newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor met Venezuela govt on CVG aluminium.
newsitem.headline: Gencor met Venezuela govt on CVG aluminium.

text.p: Gencor Ltd said on Monday it had held talks with Venezuela's president and other senior government officials last week over the group's interest in the privatisation of state-owned CVG's aluminium interests.

"A successful bid for the aluminium assets held by the state-owned company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) would significantly strengthen Gencor's existing aluminium portfolio and add to the group's substantial investments in Latin America," Gencor said in a statement.
It said it would be joined in the bid for CVG by Venezuelan company Sural with whom it signed a formal agreement last week.
Venezuela expects to sell CVG by the end of the year. CVG's assets comprise smelters Venalum and Alcasa, bauxite producer Bauxilum and carbon anode manufacturer Carbonorca.
With cheap electrical power and ready supplies of alumina ore, the complex produces over 600,000 tonnes of aluminium a year.

Gencor's aluminium assets include the 500,000 tonnes a year Hillside smelter in South Africa -- one of the largest modern smelters in the world -- and the aluminium, bauxite and alumina assets of Billiton International.
Gencor's aluminium division is one of the world's five top producers with annual output of around 900,000 tonnes.
Gencor is one of 13 companies pre-selected to bid in the auction. Others include Alcoa, Alumax, Reynolds Metal Co, Norsk Hydro ASA and RTZ Corp.
